h1.cap: Feeling alone? Machiavelli's darkest days... are when he wrote The Prince.

n2.cap: 1512. He loses his job. Then prison. Then a small farm... far from power.

n3.cap: By day... dust and neighbours. But every evening...

q1.cap: he wrote... "I pull off my peasant-clothes... and put on my noble court dress."

n4.cap: Then, with the great men of old... for four hours, he forgot every trouble.

n5.cap: The mind's answer. Being alone is an appointment... so dress for it.

n6.cap: Rumi's reed flute plays in every crowd... for the happy and the sad.

q2.cap: Yet it sighs... "each interprets my notes... but not one fathoms the secrets of my heart."

n7.cap: Lonely... in a full room. And still, that same song moves people to tears.

n8.cap: My take? Neither man hid it. One wrote it down. One sang it out. Alone isn't the end... it's raw material.

n9.cap: Tonight, one hour alone, phone in another room... and make one thing. A page. A plan. A song.

n10.cap: When you feel alone... do you reach for the book, or the flute? Tell us below.

n11.cap: Follow Awazzzz... you're less alone than you think.
